builder_plan.scenario: A support or data assistant repeats work across related customer requests.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's memory change in a replay of past tasks, with separate memory per customer.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current memory pipeline plus a no-memory control using the same agent.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, stale memories, retrieval misses, response latency, and all memory maintenance costs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: What Remains in Sight? Autoregressive Video Decoding as Representation-Guided Context Rewriting
summary: ReCR replaces implicit past-context selection (recent windows, compressed caches, external memory) in autoregressive video decoding with an explicit training-free selection of history units guided by internal decoder representations, mapped onto a compact causal axis before each block is decoded. It costs additional inference-time computation for representation extraction and selection scoring, and implementation complexity to expose decoder internals, while keeping the visible-token budget unchanged. It can fail if the backbone does not expose suitable internal representations, if the selection heuristics (global-state match, redundancy avoidance, boundary coverage, spatial diversity) misfire on the target domain, or if the quality gain does not materialize on workloads whose degradation mode differs from the evaluated benchmarks.
rationale: It is training-free and inference-time, so it fits constrained infrastructure, but its benefit must be validated on the reader's specific video backbone and workload before production adoption.
technique: Representation-guided context selection for autoregressive video decoding

claims.statement: ReCR replaces implicit past-context selection (recent windows, compressed caches, external memory) in autoregressive video decoding with an explicit training-free selection of history units guided by internal decoder representations, mapped onto a compact causal axis before each block is decoded. It costs additional inference-time computation for representation extraction and selection scoring, and implementation complexity to expose decoder internals, while keeping the visible-token budget unchanged. It can fail if the backbone does not expose suitable internal representations, if the selection heuristics (global-state match, redundancy avoidance, boundary coverage, spatial diversity) misfire on the target domain, or if the quality gain does not materialize on workloads whose degradation mode differs from the evaluated benchmarks.
Consistently improves multiple autoregressive backbones under matched visible-token budgets on long-horizon text-to-video benchmarks; no numeric factor is given in the abstract.
